meaning_fixes.after: If they start it, take it!
meaning_fixes.reason: Wrong addressee: source '売られたケンカは買いやがれ！' is the rough imperative idiom 'if a fight is sold [to you], buy it' aimed at an ally who should not back down, matching the scold sequence around it (13527 'Stop dawdling around!', 13529 'Hey, get a grip!'). The draft turned it into a taunt at the enemy ('you started it'), reversing who is being addressed. The genuinely enemy-directed, first-person form of the same idiom appears correctly later at dialogue_13540 ('Started it? I'll finish it!'), confirming the two source lines use different grammar (buiyagare, imperative to a second party vs buttte yaru ze, self-declaration to the opponent).

checked_decisions.finding: Translator's flagged compressions (Ryoko's resource 2812220) keep the core meaning and brash/hotheaded register; no dropped sentence endings or reversed meaning found.

'Counting on you, don't fail.' adds a harsher conditional ('don't fail') not literally in '頼んだぜ、頼りにしてっからな' (a plain statement of trust/reliance). This is a tone intensification consistent with Ryoko's brash character rather than an invented fact or reversal, so it is left as a phrasing choice, not fixed.
'Started it? I'll finish it!' correctly renders the first-person, opponent-directed form of the buy/sell-a-fight idiom (contrast with the ally-directed imperative form fixed at dialogue_13528).

'てめーら、無事だったか！' is literally a question ('were you all unharmed?'); the draft's declarative 'You punks made it!' shifts mood from question to statement but keeps the same concern-for-allies meaning, not a reversal. Left as is.
Hikaru Amano's 'draw person on my palm, gulp!' folk-ritual line is compressed but not misrepresented; nothing invented beyond the source gesture.
